stem: A patient requests an authorized refill of Provigil at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which schedule-based duties govern the transaction? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prescription expires five days after issue.
Schedule IV refill count and timing limits apply.
Covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
The pharmacist may create a new prescription after five refills.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Schedule IV refill count and timing limits apply. Covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: Modafinil is federally noncontrolled.
choice_analysis.B: Not supported: The prescription expires five days after issue.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Schedule IV refill count and timing limits apply.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: Covered dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
choice_analysis.E: Not supported: The pharmacist may create a new prescription after five refills.

related_facts: modafinil (Provigil) is used for improve wakefulness in narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, or shift-work disorder; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Modafinil is federally noncontrolled.'

reasoning_steps: Classify modafinil under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
